title: Edgecase Runoff: Solo-Model Onboarding Eval Notes (Jun 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This doc records the results and rationale from a narrow "runoff" evaluation used to decide whether to onboard model-ci-3.1 (quantized 4-bit variant) versus retaining model-cg-2.5 (current default) for the "edgecase" promptset. The earlier broad bakeoff showed the two families were within noise on core metrics; this runoff targets the specific failure modes and cost/latency tradeoffs we care about for production rollout.

High-level decision outcome (status: provisional):
- Candidate: model-ci-3.1 (4-bit quant, recommended for canary)
- Reason: statistically significant better preference on structured extraction prompts and 18% lower token-cost on our workload distribution with marginal latency regression within SLO for Dedicated. Caveats: minor regression on hallucination on one open-domain subset; requires narrow prompt guardrail patch.

Evaluation design summary:
- Goal: measure head-to-head preference, safety regressions, latency and unit cost under realistic traffic mixes for the "edgecase" product feature (structured Q/A, code-synthesis, and short-dialog).
- Promptsets used:
  - edgecase-core-1000: 1k human-authored edge prompts (structured extraction + adversarial paraphrases).
  - edgecase-open-200: 200 freeform user prompts that historically triggered hallucinations.
  - perf-sim-10k: sampled trace to simulate token distribution and concurrency.
- Metrics: pairwise preference (crowd A/B, 3 raters), win_rate (per prompt), mean preference score, hallucination_rate (binary per response), latency P50/P95 (ms), cost_per_1M_tokens (USD estimate using host pricing), regression_delta (relative to baseline).
- Stats: bootstrap 10k resamples for CI on win_rate; p-values from two-sided permutation test.

Leaderboards (condensed):
- Pairwise preference (edgecase-core-1000): model-ci-3.1 beat model-cg-2.5 on 572/1000 prompts (win_rate=57.2%, 95% CI [54.7, 59.6], p=0.003)
- Open prompts (edgecase-open-200): model-ci-3.1 lost 45/200 (win_rate=22.5% favoring baseline), but differences were not statistically significant (p=0.12) and concentrated in a small subset of topics (historical facts).
- Aggregate business-weighted win_rate (weighted by traffic mix): 55.1% in favor of model-ci-3.1.

Quantitative summary table (text):
- Win rate (weighted): baseline model-cg-2.5 = 44.9%, candidate model-ci-3.1 = 55.1%
- Hallucination rate (edgecase-open-200): baseline = 6.8%, candidate = 8.3% (absolute +1.5pp, relative +22%)
- Latency P50 (perf-sim-10k): baseline = 82ms, candidate = 95ms (+13ms, +15.9%)
- Latency P95 (perf-sim-10k): baseline = 278ms, candidate = 330ms (+52ms, +18.7%)
- Estimated token cost (hosted pricing model, per 1M tokens): baseline = $1,420, candidate = $1,164 (-18%)
- Significance notes: win_rate CI does not overlap at 95% for core prompts; hallucination delta CI overlaps zero at 90% for full sample but not for the historic-facts subset.

Win/Loss breakdown (examples):
- Wins for model-ci-3.1: extraction tasks with long lists where 3.1 reliably produced correct tabular outputs; code completion prompts that required precise return types; prompts where brevity and conservative defaults were valued.
- Losses for model-ci-3.1: open-domain fact checks and multi-step historical reasoning where model-cg-2.5 preserved context slightly better (qualitative: more hedging and citation-like phrasing).

Failure-case archetypes identified:
1) Fact-stamp drift: candidate produced confident but incorrect short facts for a narrow set of 26 prompts (mostly date/place queries). Root cause hypothesis: quantized weights reduce rare-token emission calibration for named entities. Mitigation: add prompt prefix that forces citation style or trigger hybrid fallback to baseline for identified topics.
2) Tokenization edge effects: certain multi-token code identifiers caused minor truncation in generated signatures. Fix: update tokenizer mapping in preprocessing pipeline; additional unit test added.
3) Long-list truncation: candidate sometimes omitted final list items under tight max-tokens; solution: tweak generation params (allow small prefix cache bump) and re-run.

Operational considerations:
- Canary plan: 2-week canary on Dedicated capacity with 5% traffic split, route non-critical routes first (structured extraction). Include live chat for CS to flag regressions.
- Fallback policy: immediate fallback to model-cg-2.5 on detected hallucination pattern (regex-based entity mismatches) and on tokenization errors.
- Monitoring hooks to add: per-prompt topic drift tracker, hallucination rate by topic, latency SLO alerts at P95 > 350ms, cost burn monitor for token usage.

Recommendation and proposed rollout steps:
1) Approve canary for model-ci-3.1 with the conditional guardrails above.
2) Implement two prompt-engineering patches before canary: (a) citation-preface for historical facts, (b) safe-list mapping for critical entity tokens.
3) Run focused re-eval after patch on the 26 failing fact prompts; require hallucination delta <= +0.5pp versus baseline before expanding canary to 20% traffic.
4) If re-eval still shows regression, run a targeted hybrid policy: route historical-fact topic to model-cg-2.5, everything else to model-ci-3.1.

Open questions for the next sync:
- Is the +18% latency P95 acceptable for Dedicated customers at current SLOs? (SRE input needed)
- Do we want to accept a small hallucination uptick in exchange for 18% cost savings? (Product & Legal input on user-facing risk)
- Could we tighten quantization to 5-bit for named-entity stability with similar cost benefits? (Research experiment to run)

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes
- Eval commit: model-registry@v2026-06-12 (see linked GitHub PR).
- Human eval batches: HT-4542 (3 raters per pair, qualification pass rate 89%).
- Scripts: eval/edgecase/run_pairwise.sh --prompts edgecase-core-1000 --seed 42 --bootstrap 10000
- Quick links: JIRA MLON-4321 for rollout, Confluence page for raw CSVs, GH PR for tokenizer fix branch.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc mixes formal numbers and working hypotheses; please call out if you want the raw CSVs or the per-topic disaggregation.
- If product decides cost is higher priority, we can also try a small temperature/brevity tweak that reduces tokens but may reduce preference scores on creative prompts.

Signed off (provisional):
Aisha Patel (applied ML), Marco Nguyen (eval leads), Ellen Ramos (product), Priya Sinha (SRE review pending)
